title: Pakistan to Host 2027 SCO Summit in Islamabad, Raising Question of Modi Visit
excerpt: As Pakistan prepares to host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit next year, diplomatic observers are watching whether India-Pakistan tensions will prevent PM Modi from attending.
body:
• Pakistan will host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation heads-of-state summit in Islamabad in 2027, as announced by PM Shehbaz Sharif
  • As rotating chair, Pakistan is obligated to invite all SCO member state leaders, including Indian PM Narendra Modi
  • India-Pakistan relations remain frozen since the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 people
  • At the 2025 Tianjin SCO summit, Modi and Sharif were both present but held no bilateral meeting

Pakistan is gearing up to host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation heads-of-state summit in Islamabad in 2027, a diplomatic event that will force the question of whether Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will set foot on Pakistani soil amid the worst bilateral tensions in years.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced the hosting plans in September 2025, directing authorities to begin infrastructure preparations in the capital, including new accommodations for visiting dignitaries and beautification projects across Islamabad.

Diplomatic Protocol Meets Political Reality

As the rotating chair of the SCO, Pakistan is required to invite all heads of state from the bloc's 10 member nations. That includes Modi, whose government has maintained a near-total freeze on high-level engagement with Islamabad since the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack in Indian-administered Kashmir that killed 26 people, mostly tourists.

India subsequently suspended the Indus Waters Treaty, a foundational agreement between the two nations signed in 1960, escalating the diplomatic fallout.

"We need to begin preparations now."

— Shehbaz Sharif, Prime Minister of Pakistan

Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Mumtaz Zahra Baloch had previously confirmed that invitations would be sent to all SCO member state leaders, including the Indian prime minister, though without specifying whether a bilateral meeting would be sought.

Tianjin Summit Set the Tone

The dynamics were on display at the most recent SCO summit in Tianjin, China, in August-September 2025, where Modi and Sharif were both present but held no bilateral meeting. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stated at the time that "Pakistan will not beg for talks" but remained open to "composite dialogue in a dignified and respectful manner."

India, for its part, made clear that meaningful engagement was contingent on Pakistan addressing cross-border terrorism. Modi used the Tianjin forum to call for "global unity against terrorism" directly in Sharif's presence, a pointed message that drew broad SCO support.

The Tianjin joint declaration condemned the Pahalgam attack and endorsed India's position that "double standards" on terrorism are unacceptable.

Stakes for 2027

The 2027 summit carries higher stakes than a typical SCO rotation. It would mark the first time Pakistan has hosted an SCO heads-of-state summit, and a Modi visit to Islamabad would be symbolically significant — no Indian prime minister has visited Pakistan since Narendra Modi's surprise stopover in Lahore in December 2015.

For India's diaspora, the India-Pakistan diplomatic trajectory affects everything from regional security perceptions to travel and trade corridors. A Modi visit to Pakistan, however unlikely it may seem now, would represent a dramatic shift in the subcontinent's geopolitical landscape.

The 2026 SCO summit, meanwhile, is scheduled for August 31 to September 1 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, with all member states expected to attend.
